ev.q: identified 54 cases of pesticide-related illnesses associated with automatic insecticide dispensers
signs and symptoms for 36 (38%) involved the eye; 34 (36%), the neurologic system
Thirty-five (81%) of these cases were in persons exposed while at work
During 1986--1999, 43 cases of acute pesticide-related illnesses associated with automatic insecticide dispensers were reported

public_health_question.v: What illnesses are associated with automatic insecticide dispensers, and under what circumstances do they occur?

ev.q: This report describes cases, summarizes surveillance data for pesticide-related illnesses associated with automatic insecticide dispensers
Illnesses Associated With Use of Automatic Insecticide Dispenser Units
surveillance data were reviewed to identify additional cases of pesticide-related illnesses
TESS is maintained by the American Association of Poison Control Centers
reported to CDPR (32 cases), MDA (four cases), FDH (three cases), NPTN (two cases), and WSDH (two cases)
Data were provided by the Toxic Exposure Surveillance System (TESS)

equity.level_reason: Only age and sex of cases are described, with no social-position framing.

ev.q: the median age was 22.5 years (range: 3--73 years)
Among the 53 cases for which sex was known, 27 (50%) were male.

notes: Four case reports plus descriptive tallies from poison-center and state surveillance data; TESS and non-TESS data were checked for overlap (a duplicate check, not a comparison).
